description: Mountain passes are natural navigable routes through mountain ranges that facilitate travel, trade, and navigation. Mountain peaks are the highest points (summits) of mountains, holding significant geographical and topographical importance.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: Fundamental geographical terminology related to mountains, passes, and topography.

key_concepts.explanation: A naturally occurring gap or navigable route through a mountain range or over a ridge, traditionally used for transportation, trade, and military movements.
The topmost pointed part of a mountain, also commonly referred to as a summit.
A continuous chain or series of mountains and hills closely related in position, direction, and geological origin.

sections.title: Major Mountain Peaks of India and the World
sections.description: Crucial mountain peaks from an exam perspective, detailing their heights and geographical locations.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: The highest peak in the world (8,848.86 m). It is known as 'Sagarmatha' in Nepal and 'Chomolungma' in Tibet.
The highest peak of India and the second-highest peak in the world (8,611 m).
The highest undisputed peak located entirely within India's territory (8,586 m) and the third-highest globally.
The highest peak of Peninsular India and the Western Ghats (2,695 m).
The highest peak of the ancient Aravalli Range (1,722 m), located in Mount Abu.

sections.title: Major Mountain Passes of North India
sections.description: Important passes located in the Himalayan region and their connecting routes.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: The highest pass in India, serving as a vital link connecting India and China.
Connects Srinagar to Leh. It is a crucial part of National Highway 1 (NH-1).
Connects the Kullu Valley with the Lahaul and Spiti Valleys.
Part of the ancient Silk Route, it connects Sikkim to Tibet via the Chumbi Valley.
The Sutlej River enters India through this pass. It connects Shimla to Tibet.

sections.title: Passes of Northeast and Peninsular India
sections.description: Passes of strategic and commercial importance located in the Eastern Himalayas and the Western Ghats.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Provides a strategic route connecting Tawang (Arunachal Pradesh) to Lhasa, the capital of Tibet.
An important mountain pass that connects Mumbai to Nashik.
A crucial transport artery that connects Mumbai to Pune.
Located between the Nilgiri and Annamalai hills, it connects the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

sections.title: Quick Matching: Passes and Peaks
sections.description: Direct one-to-one mapping of important geographical locations and their unique features.

key_associations.extra_info: The famous Jawahar Tunnel is located under this pass, connecting Jammu to Srinagar.
These passes connect the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand to Tibet.
An important strategic pass that connects Imphal (India) to Myanmar.
The second-highest peak located entirely within the geographical borders of India.
The highest peak on the African continent and a dormant volcano.

sections.title: Important Facts
sections.description: Specific one-liner facts related to mountains and passes that are frequently asked in exams.

important_facts.fact: Bachendri Pal made history by becoming the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest in 1984.
The highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills is Doddabetta, standing at an elevation of 2,637 meters.
The highest point of the Satpura Range is Dhupgarh (1,350 m), located in the state of Madhya Pradesh.
The highest peak in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is Saddle Peak, with an elevation of 732 meters.
Lipulekh Pass, located in Uttarakhand, is the primary land route used by Hindu pilgrims for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra.
